A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same selective-inference study, and their text, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The original EEG appendix, Appendix F, is retained as Appendix H in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic error-rate and power experiments, EEG saliency tests, and robustness and modified-EEG experiments in Section 6 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds threshold-sensitivity and architecture/saliency-method evaluations in Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The subgraph selection, test statistic, conditioning, and parametric-programming procedure remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. Appendix G applies the existing framework to additional GNN and saliency configurations rather than introducing a new inference component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic graph distributions, non-Gaussian noise families, RSVP EEG dataset, and modified-EEG scenarios. The added threshold and model-configuration experiments do not introduce new datasets, populations, or task requirements.

E2.justification: The synthetic comparisons retain naive, Bonferroni, and w/o-pp; the EEG comparisons retain proposed versus naive. Appendix G's architecture/saliency combinations are configurations evaluated using the proposed test, not additional competing inference methods.

E3.justification: The original synthetic and EEG protocols remain intact. New experiments sweep ten valid threshold pairs and evaluate GCN+GradCAM, GIN+Grad, and GIN+GradInput. Appendix G specifies second-layer Grad-CAM and three-layer GINs with 64-dimensional representations under the existing synthetic evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendices F–G add substantial checks of two previously untested applicability boundaries: sensitivity to threshold choices and error control beyond GCN+CAM. Figures 8–9 provide the corresponding evidence. Existing non-Gaussian, estimated-variance, w/o-pp, and EEG analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 simulated tests per synthetic setting and display error bars. The new experiments inherit the existing protocol; no changed repetition counts, seed disclosures, error-bar definitions, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Figures 8–9 substantially extend the reported validation, showing Type I error rates near the nominal 0.05 across tested threshold pairs and additional GNN/saliency configurations. Existing Figure 3 curves, EEG p-values, and robustness and modified-EEG results are retained; no same-setting performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: The statistical definitions, assumptions, Lemmas 1–2, Theorem 1, and appendix proofs and interval derivations are unchanged. Appendix G's standard GIN update equation documents an experimental architecture rather than adding or revising the inferential theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains exact, Type-I-error-controlled testing of GNN saliency. The introduction now explicitly focuses on discovering input-data structure and states that statistical significance is insufficient for interpretability, modestly qualifying the reliability claim.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds substantive distinctions between statistical plausibility and fidelity, consistency, completeness, and simplicity. It explains the additional conditioning needed for adaptive thresholds and expands supported and unsupported architecture/explainer boundaries. Section 6.3 and Figure 4 add P300 timing and scalp-location interpretations of existing EEG examples.

D1.justification: v1 states that code is supplementary material; v2 supplies a specific repository address. Appendix G adds implementation details for the evaluated GINs, including MLP dimensions, learned epsilon, pooling, and classification layers, and identifies the layer used for Grad-CAM.

R1.justification: Six references are added concerning GINs, graph attention, gradient attribution, image-segmentation selective inference, and interpretability evaluation. These refine applicability and complementary-metric positioning, while the existing related-work discussion and principal novelty claim remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract and introduction edits, expands scope and EEG explanations, and adds a Broader Impact section and Appendices F–G. Author-contact formatting and section-reference wording also change. The main narrative sequence and most technical prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the threshold-grid Figure 8 and configuration-comparison Figure 9, enlarges Figure 3 and corrects its column description, and expands Figure 4's caption. Existing EEG figures are repositioned or renumbered, with their plotted content retained.

improvement.justification: The added threshold and architecture checks strengthen support for the existing validity claim, while Section 5 better explains interpretability and applicability limits. The repository address and implementation details also improve reproducibility. These are useful but bounded gains: empirical coverage remains unchanged, and Section 6.3 still reverses the positive/negative p-value pattern shown in Figures 4–5.
